components.description: Unpaid family leave under the FMLA of up to 12 weeks per July-June year, for the birth of a child, adoption or foster placement, care of a seriously ill spouse, child, domestic partner or parent, or the extension of a medical leave; job and benefits protected.
components.faculty_group_note: Policy 204-03 applies to all Rice University tenured and tenure-track faculty; 'Family leave under the Family and Medical Leave Act for faculty'
components.eligible_parent_wording: birth of a child of the faculty member; placement of a child with the faculty member for adoption or foster care; care for a spouse, child, domestic partner or parent; extension of a medical leave
components.entitlement_note: A statutory leave (FMLA) is coded guaranteed (checklist, entitlement). The policy says 'may be granted' but also 'is granted upon request with appropriate documentation'.

notes: Governing document: Policy 204-03 (last revised 2003-02-11, captured 2018-04-20), applies to all tenured and tenure-track faculty. The Faculty Handbook chapter IX (capture 2016-10-24, outside the reference year, footer (c)2014) is a faculty guide that defers to University Policies; it is used only for supporting detail and agrees with Policy 204-03. Policy 201 (revised 2016-05-12) governs tenure-clock effects; its s.7.b defers to Policy 204 for medical leaves.

Birth parent chain: medical leave for pregnancy and childbirth (c3, no stated length, discretionary) with short-term disability pay within it (c4), long-term disability after (c5) -> primary caregiver leave, 1 semester at full pay if primary caregiver (c2, also_available with c3, within 9 months) ; FMLA 12 weeks (c1) concurrent_with c3 and c2, starting with the earliest.
Non-birth parent chain: primary caregiver leave, 1 semester at full pay, if the primary caregiver (c2); FMLA 12 weeks (c1) concurrent_with it. c3-c5 do not count for this role.
Primary caregiver leave: only one person per child may be primary caregiver (one entitlement per child, not divided); figures assume the member is the primary caregiver (R6).
Handbook IX.C.3: Rice continues to pay its portion of benefits for up to twelve months of leave; not a component (benefit continuation, not leave or pay).
Professional leaves (Policy 208) and military leave (Policy 418-93) are not usable for a birth; not components. Junior research leave (Policy 201 s.3.b.4) is not a parental provision.
